sentences.text: The only known specimen of Proceratosaurus is a mostly complete skull with a lower jaw and hyoid bone. This holotype — the specimen the species is based on — measures 26.9 cm in length as preserved. The skull features an infratemporal fenestra that is narrow, elongate, kidney-shaped, and around 5.4 cm tall.

Estimates for the animal's size vary. A 2010 redescription estimated the holotype individual to be 2.98 to 3.16 meters long and weigh between 28 and 36 kilograms. Other sources have estimated the length to be between 3 and 4 meters and its body mass to be between 50 and 100 kilograms.
Proceratosaurus was first described in 1910 and reclassified into its own genus in 1926. The fossil was discovered by F. Lewis Bradley and described by Arthur Smith Woodward in 1910.
The holotype specimen has been housed at the Natural History Museum in London since 1942. Oliver Rauhut and colleagues re-described the skull in 2010.

Proceratosaurus is classified as a coelurosaur in the family Proceratosauridae. It was likely a carnivore that ate relatively small prey. Researchers suggest that Proceratosaurus likely fed on small-bodied prey based on its low bite force and skull morphology.
The cranial crest of Proceratosaurus was likely used for display. Rauhut and colleagues suggest that the prominent head crest of Proceratosaurus was likely used as a display feature.
Proceratosaurus was originally classified as the species Megalosaurus bradleyi.

In the 1930s, von Huene suggested that Proceratosaurus was closely related to Ceratosaurus and considered both to be members of Coelurosauria. In 1988, Paul suggested that Proceratosaurus was a close relative of Ornitholestes, primarily due to the presence of a nasal crest. A 1998 phylogenetic analysis by Thomas R. Holtz Jr. classified Proceratosaurus as a basal coelurosaur.

Proceratosaurus lived during the Middle Jurassic, specifically the Bathonian age. Proceratosaurus lived in what is now England during the Middle Jurassic. Fossils of Proceratosaurus are found in the White Limestone Formation or the Forest Marble Formation of the Great Oolite Group in England.
Proceratosaurus is closely related to the tyrannosauroid Guanlong from the Late Jurassic of China.
It was debated whether Piveteausaurus divesensis belonged to Proceratosaurus, but later research rejected this suggestion.
